title: T1052 — Exfiltration Over Physical Medium
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Exfiltration Over Physical Medium with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: A normal Tuesday
steps.caption: The office local area network (LAN) is idle. Only routine traffic moves between the workstation and the file server, drawn as slow background dots on the top edge. The SOC / DLP console node sits quiet: no device events, no DLP alerts, nothing unusual at all
steps.defender: Physical, DHCP, NAC and network-flow records connect the asset to the activity.

steps.title: Sensitive files are staged
steps.caption: Dots flow from the file server down to the workstation. The insider runs a small script that packs the R&D folder into a password-protected archive at C:\Users\ \AppData\Local\Temp\helpdesk_cache.zip using 7-Zip. The defender sees the first-ever use of 7z.exe on this host (Sysmon EID 1, where EID means event ID) and a file-create event for the archive (Sysmon EID 11)

steps.title: A USB drive appears
steps.caption: The insider plugs a personal stick into the workstation. Windows writes a key under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USBSTOR and fires driver install events 20001/20003 in Microsoft-Windows-DriverFrameworks-UserMode. The device-control agent records the serial number and friendly name of the new storage device
